cases.comment: Prepare the PDB for tleap: Write a cleaned copy of the input first: hydrogens removed (tleap rebuilds them), TER records between chains, first MODEL only. Rosetta / FARFAR2 models need this.
Remove 5′-terminal phosphates: Drop P/OP1/OP2 of each chain's first residue: Amber's 5′-terminal residues (G5, A5 ...) have no phosphate.
Break chains at numbering gaps: Insert a TER record where residue numbers jump, so tleap does not bond across a gap.
Remove waters from the input: Crystal waters are dropped; the solvent box is built by tleap.

RNA force field: leaprc file for RNA. 'OL3 + CP' adds the phosphate oxygen vdW correction of Steinbrecher et al. (JCTC 2012) from the frcmod below; NBfix19 / 0BPh assume it. Choices: ol3cp, ol3, ljbb, roc, yil, shaw.

CP parameters: Retyped library: the build script writes RNA_CP.lib (AmberTools' RNA.lib with the phosphate oxygens retyped OP / OR) and frcmod.cp (the CP Lennard-Jones values plus the parm10.dat bonded terms for the new types), so only phosphate oxygens change and the NBfix19 / 0BPh masks address them as @%OP / @%OR. Own frcmod: load a CP parameter file you provide (masks stay @%O2 / @%OS). Choices: lib, frcmod.
CP frcmod file: Parameter file with the CP phosphate correction: a name in leap's search path / the step folder, or an absolute path.
Extra parameter files: One frcmod file per line, loaded with loadamberparams after the force field (e.g. frcmod.LRNA).
Extra residue libraries: One library (.lib / .off) per line, loaded with loadOff (e.g. LRNA.lib).
Leap commands before parameter files: Inserted right after the leaprc files, e.g. addAtomTypes for new atom types.
Leap commands before loadpdb: Inserted before the PDB is read, e.g. addPdbResMap entries.
Leap commands after loadpdb: Inserted after the PDB is read and before solvation, e.g. bond commands.
Water model: Water model; its leaprc also loads the matching monovalent / divalent ion parameters. Choices: spce, tip3p, opc, opc3, tip4pew, fb3, tip4pd, tip4p2005, none.
Box shape: Truncated octahedron (solvateoct) needs ~30 % less water than a rectangular box. Choices: oct, rect, cubic.
Buffer: Minimum distance between the RNA and the box edge.
Neutralise with monovalent cations: addIonsRand <cation> 0 neutralises the RNA's phosphate charge.
Cation: Monovalent cation for neutralisation and salt. Choices: Na+, K+.
Mg²⁺ ions: Number of Mg²⁺ ions (residue MG) added at random positions.
Balance Mg²⁺ with Cl⁻: Add two Cl⁻ per Mg²⁺ so the box stays neutral.
Extra salt pairs: Additional cation/Cl⁻ pairs (≈ concentration [M] × number of waters / 55.5).

Mg²⁺ Lennard-Jones model: 12-6: the Li & Merz parameters loaded with the water model. 12-6-4 (Li & Merz): loads frcmod.ions234lm_1264_<water> and adds the C4 terms with ParmEd add12_6_4 (Amber only; GROMACS cannot represent C4). microMg / nanoMg (Grotz, Cruz-León & Schwierz): optimised 12-6 Mg²⁺ with explicit Mg²⁺-RNA pair terms tuned to phosphate binding - written as a frcmod plus ParmEd changeLJPair lines, and carried into GROMACS as [ nonbond_params ]. microMg keeps the experimental (µs) water exchange; nanoMg exchanges water faster for better sampling of ion binding. Choices: 126, 1264, micro, nano.

Mg²⁺-Cl⁻ pair term: Apply the authors' Mg²⁺-Cl⁻ pair term (optimised with their Cl⁻ model; Amber's Cl⁻ parameters are kept for everything else). Without it Mg²⁺-Cl⁻ follows the combination rule with the optimised Mg²⁺, which is not a published combination and gives much too strong Mg²⁺-Cl⁻ contacts.
NBfix19 (gHBfix19 as LJ pairs): Off-diagonal Lennard-Jones terms for -NH...N- and -OH...O(phosphate) pairs (Kuehrova & Mlynsky JCTC 2019; Mlynsky et al. 2026). The masks assume OL3 + CP.
0BPh pairs: Extra H5/H4 – O5' Lennard-Jones pairs of the 0BPh modification (Mlýnský et al. 2023): masks @%OR with the CP library, @%OS otherwise.

Separate HO and O2 Lennard-Jones types first: addLJType @%HO and @%O2 before the pair changes. tleap merges atom types with equal LJ parameters: HO shares its LJ type with water HW and O2 with base carbonyl O, so without this the HO-O2 / HO-OS pairs also change water-H and carbonyl-O interactions.
Hydrogen mass repartitioning: ParmEd HMassRepartition (hydrogens 3.024 Da) so MD can use a 4 fs time step with SHAKE.
Extra ParmEd commands: Added before outparm, e.g. the L-RNA changeLJPair lines.

Name L-nucleotides for leap: Before tleap, residues whose sugar chirality (C1'/C3'/C4') is L get L-RNA names (Dudek & Trylska: LA LC LG LU, terminals LA5/LA3 ...), the other RNA residues Amber names. Runs the PDB tools that MDATK copies into the step folder (replaces to_lrna.sh); a structure without L residues is only checked.
Force L for: Residues that are L whatever their geometry says (overrides the detection), e.g. 'C:45-73', 'A:45-73, A:80-90' or 'C' for a whole chain.
5'/3' terminal names: LA5/LA3 ... at chain ends as in nucleic12_LRNA.lib. Off: plain LA/LC/LG/LU at the ends (as to_lrna.sh wrote), for libraries that map terminals with addPdbResMap.

NBfix19 / 0BPh / CP for L-RNA: Declare the L-RNA library's atom types for tleap (addAtomTypes) and add the NBfix19 / 0BPh pairs for its bridging-oxygen type (HO, H5, H4 against LD, as for OS / OR in D-RNA). ParmEd skips them when the structure has no L residues. The CP correction of L residues comes with the L-RNA parameter file (e.g. frcmod.LRNA).
L-RNA atom types: Atom types of the L-RNA library declared as sp3 oxygens before it is loaded; the first one is the bridging phosphate oxygen used in the NBfix19 / 0BPh pairs.
Two-pass build: L-RNA naming -> dry tleap -> ParmEd -> ambpdb -> solvated tleap -> ParmEd. The ambpdb PDB keeps the dry topology's residue names (Amber terminal names are re-applied).
Also save a PDB of the built system: tleap savepdb after solvation - handy for a visual check.
Conda environment: Activate this conda environment at the top of the script (eval "$(conda shell.bash hook)"; conda activate <name>). Leave empty when the programs are already on PATH.
Setup commands: Shell lines run before any program, e.g. 'module load ...' on a cluster or 'source /opt/amber26/amber.sh' on a workstation.
Sequence: RNA sequence in topology order; chains separated by spaces, '&' or new lines (optionally 'A: GGCAC...'). Not needed when a secondary-structure file is connected.
Secondary structure: Dot-bracket notation for the whole sequence; '()', '[]', '{}' and '<>' pairs are restrained. Strand separators (spaces, '&') are ignored.
Residue offset: Topology residue number = position in the sequence + offset (use when the topology has extra residues before the RNA).
Restrain G·U wobble pairs: Also restrain G·U pairs (G O6–U N3, G N1–U O2). Off: only Watson–Crick G–C and A–U pairs are restrained.
r1: Lower distance where the linear restraint wall starts (Å).
r2: Start of the flat bottom (Å).
r3: End of the flat bottom (Å).
r4: Upper distance where the restraint turns linear (Å).
rk2: Force constant below r2 (kcal/mol/Å²).
rk3: Force constant above r3 (kcal/mol/Å²).
Conda environment: Activate this conda environment at the top of the script (eval "$(conda shell.bash hook)"; conda activate <name>). Leave empty when the programs are already on PATH.
Setup commands: Shell lines run before any program, e.g. 'module load ...' on a cluster or 'source /opt/amber26/amber.sh' on a workstation.
MD engine: Program for the MD stages. Choices: pmemd.cuda, pmemd, pmemd.MPI.
Amber version: Version the files target (local Amber 26 or cluster Amber 24); the input format is the same, the version is recorded in the scripts. Choices: 26, 24.
MPI processes: Processes for pmemd.MPI.
MPI launcher: Command placed before pmemd.MPI; {n} is replaced by the process count (srun on SLURM clusters).
GPU (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES): Optional GPU index for pmemd.cuda.
Minimisation engine: pmemd.cuda can stop on bad initial contacts; the CPU pmemd is more forgiving. Choices: same, pmemd.
Input coordinates have velocities: Tick when the starting rst7 is a restart of an earlier MD run, so the first MD stage can continue it (irest=1).
Positional restraint reference: Coordinates used as -ref for positional restraints. Choices: previous, initial.
Separate production script: Production stages go into their own script (e.g. to run them on a cluster).
Skip finished stages: When the script is re-run, stages whose output file already has pmemd's final timing lines are skipped (resumes an interrupted run).
Stages run in order; each starts from the previous stage's restart file.
Name: Short stage name used in file names (letters, digits, hyphens), e.g. min1, heat, eq, prod.
Title: First line of the mdin file (a free comment).
Type: Energy minimisation (imin=1) or molecular dynamics (imin=0). Choices: min, md.
Cycles (maxcyc): Total minimisation cycles.
Steepest-descent cycles (ncyc): With ntmin=1: cycles of steepest descent before switching to conjugate gradient.
Method (ntmin): Minimisation algorithm. Choices: 1, 2, 0.
Steps (nstlim): Number of MD steps.
Time step (dt): Time step in ps (0.002 with SHAKE; 0.004 needs hydrogen mass repartitioning).
Velocities: auto: new velocities (irest=0, ntx=1) after a minimisation or at the start, otherwise continue the previous stage (irest=1, ntx=5). Choices: auto, new, continue.
Ensemble: Constant volume (ntb=1) or constant pressure (ntb=2, ntp>0). Choices: nvt, npt.
Thermostat: Temperature control (ntt). Choices: langevin, berendsen, andersen.
Collision frequency (gamma_ln): Langevin collision frequency in ps⁻¹.
Coupling time (tautp): Berendsen thermostat time constant (ps).
Randomisation interval (vrand): Andersen: steps between velocity randomisations.
Initial temperature (tempi): Temperature of the new velocities (K).
Temperature (temp0): Reference temperature (K).
Ramp the temperature: Raise temp0 linearly from tempi with an nmropt TEMP0 schedule instead of jumping to temp0 at once.
Ramp length (steps): Steps over which the temperature rises; the rest of the stage runs at temp0.
Barostat: Pressure control in NPT. Choices: berendsen, mc.
Pressure (pres0): Reference pressure (bar).
Relaxation time (taup): Berendsen barostat time constant (ps).
MC volume moves every (mcbarint): Steps between Monte Carlo volume moves.
Pressure scaling (ntp): Isotropic (ntp=1) or anisotropic (ntp=2). Choices: 1, 2.
SHAKE bonds to hydrogen: ntc=2, ntf=2 (needed for dt > 0.001 ps).
SHAKE tolerance (tol): Relative SHAKE tolerance; empty uses Amber's default (1.0e-5).
Random seed (ig): Empty: a new seed each run (ig=-1).
Cutoff (cut): Direct-space non-bonded cutoff (Å).
Positional restraints: Harmonic restraints to the reference coordinates (ntr=1, restraint_wt, restraintmask).
Restraint mask: Amber mask of restrained atoms; empty restrains the solute (':1-N' when the residue count is known, otherwise everything except water and ions).
Restraint weight: restraint_wt in kcal/mol/Å².
Helix distance restraints: nmropt=1 with DISANG=<restraint file> (the step's restraint input).
Print restraint violations (LISTOUT=POUT): Writes the restraint violation summary to the output file.
Energy output every (ntpr): Steps between energy printouts.
Trajectory frame every (ntwx): Steps between trajectory frames (0: no trajectory).
Restart file every (ntwr): Steps between restart-file updates.
NetCDF trajectory (ioutfm=1): Binary NetCDF instead of ASCII.
Wrap into the box (iwrap=1): Wrap molecules into the primary box in the output.
Split into segments: Run this stage as N consecutive pmemd runs (e.g. to fit cluster wall-time limits); file names get -001, -002 ...
Production stage: Its trajectory is passed on to analysis / visualisation steps and goes into the separate production script.
Extra &cntrl settings: Additional name=value settings added inside &cntrl (they override generated values with the same name).
Extra namelists: Text added after &cntrl, e.g. an &ewald namelist.
Dry PDB before production: cpptraj strips water and ions from the last restart of the main script (before the production script) - for a visual check of the equilibrated structure.
Strip mask: cpptraj mask of atoms removed in the dry PDB / trajectory.
Dry, imaged production trajectory: cpptraj autoimage + strip of the production trajectories (and the matching dry topology) for visualisation.
Strip mask (trajectory): cpptraj mask removed from the dry trajectory.
Conda environment: Activate this conda environment at the top of the script (eval "$(conda shell.bash hook)"; conda activate <name>). Leave empty when the programs are already on PATH.
Setup commands: Shell lines run before any program, e.g. 'module load ...' on a cluster or 'source /opt/amber26/amber.sh' on a workstation.
Build: Ideal helix: a new A-form duplex or single strand. Mutate: swap bases of the connected PDB. Fit: place the connected PDB in the map. Choices: helix, mutate, fit.
Sequence (5'->3'): Strand 1; T is read as U.
Partner strand: Complement (the canonical partners of the pairing: Watson-Crick for wc), none (single strand) or a sequence typed below. Choices: auto, none, explicit.
Partner (5'->3'): Same length as strand 1; mismatches and G·U wobbles are allowed (reported).

Pairing: Base-pair geometry of the duplex: Watson-Crick (antiparallel A-form, default), reverse Watson-Crick / Hoogsteen / Hoogsteen-Hoogsteen (parallel strands) or reverse Hoogsteen (antiparallel). For the Hoogsteen pairings strand 1 is the purine strand. Choices: wc, reverse-wc, hoogsteen, reverse-hoogsteen, hh.
Triplex: A third strand in the major groove on the Hoogsteen edge of the strand-1 purines (Watson-Crick duplex only). Choices: none, hoogsteen, reverse-hoogsteen.
Third strand: The canonical motif bases (U / C+ or A / G on A / G) or a sequence typed below. Choices: auto, explicit.
Third strand (5'->3'): Same length as strand 1; mismatches are allowed (reported).
Chirality: D: right-handed. L: the mirror image (left-handed, L-nucleotides). Choices: D, L.
Chain ids: Strand 1, strand 2 (and 3 of a triplex; default C).
First residue (strand 1)
First residue (strand 2)
First residue (strand 3)
Residue names: Name scheme of mdatk.pdbtools. Choices: , amber, ccd, rosetta, pdb.
5'/3' terminal names: For the schemes with terminal variants (Amber, CCD).
5'-phosphate: Keep P/OP1/OP2/OP3 on the 5' ends (the Amber 5' units have none).
Hydrogens: Add all hydrogens (default: heavy atoms only).
Mutations: Chain:residue + new base, comma separated.
Compensatory partner mutations: Change the Watson-Crick / G·U partner of every mutated base to the complement unless it is mutated explicitly.
Keep G·U pairs: A G or U facing U / G keeps its partner (wobble) instead of the Watson-Crick complement.
Map resolution: Width of the simulated model map.
Search: Global: all orientations and positions. Local: refine the model as placed. Choices: global, local.
Angular step: Rotation sampling of the global search.
Conda environment: Activate this conda environment at the top of the script (eval "$(conda shell.bash hook)"; conda activate <name>). Leave empty when the programs are already on PATH.
Setup commands: Shell lines run before any program, e.g. 'module load ...' on a cluster or 'source /opt/amber26/amber.sh' on a workstation.
Python: Interpreter that can import MDATK. From the standalone AppImage / Windows build the script calls that program itself instead.
Program: acedrg (CCP4) or phenix.elbow (Phenix) builds the restraints from the SMILES; MDATK then renames the atoms to the CCD names the model uses. Choices: acedrg, phenix.elbow.
Phenix version: Installed Phenix release. Choices: 1.21, 2.x.
Phenix installation: Top folder of the Phenix installation; the script sources its phenix_env.sh. Leave empty when phenix.elbow is already on PATH.
CCP4 setup script: Sourced before acedrg runs (ccp4.setup-sh of the CCP4 installation). Leave empty when acedrg is already on PATH.
Extra arguments: Added to every acedrg / phenix.elbow command line.

Residues: Model: the 5'/3' variants the connected model needs (all eight when no model is connected or it does not exist yet). The four parents 0A/0C/0G/0U are CCD entries that Coot and Phenix already know. Choices: auto, variants, all, list.
Codes: Residue codes separated by spaces or commas; codes that are not in the table need a custom SMILES.

Polymer group: _chem_comp.group of the dictionaries. RNA lets Coot / Phenix link the residue to its neighbours like the CCD's L-nucleotides; non-polymer makes it a free ligand. Choices: RNA, non-polymer.

Custom SMILES: One 'code = SMILES' per line. For a code of the table the SMILES replaces the built-in one and must describe the same molecule and stereochemistry; other codes keep the atom names the program invents.

Fetch SMILES from PubChem when writing (network): Off: no network access. On: the isomeric SMILES of the compounds below is downloaded from PubChem (PUG REST) when the step's files are written, checked against the code's atom graph and stereochemistry, and used instead of the built-in SMILES.
PubChem compounds: One 'code = CID' (or compound name) per line.
Timeout: Seconds to wait for PubChem.
Conda environment: Activate this conda environment at the top of the script (eval "$(conda shell.bash hook)"; conda activate <name>). Leave empty when the programs are already on PATH.
Setup commands: Shell lines run before any program, e.g. 'module load ...' on a cluster or 'source /opt/amber26/amber.sh' on a workstation.
Sequence: One chain per line or chains separated by spaces / '&' (optionally 'A: ggcac...'). Residues are numbered continuously across chains.
Write FASTA and secstruct from the fields below: Generate the Rosetta FASTA (one entry per chain, lower case, A:1-16 numbering) and the secstruct file. Off: use existing files.
Secondary structure: Dot-bracket for the whole sequence (strand separators optional). Paired bases must be complementary (G–C, A–U, G–U) or rna_denovo stops.
FASTA name: Name on the FASTA header lines; empty uses the project name.
Existing FASTA: FASTA file to use instead.
Existing secstruct: Secondary structure file to use instead (dot-bracket on line 1).
Models per run (-nstruct): Models written by each run.
Monte Carlo cycles (-cycles): Fragment-assembly cycles per model (Rosetta default 10 000).
Full-atom refinement (-minimize_rna): High-resolution minimisation after assembly - strongly recommended.
Fixed stems (-fixed_stems): Seed every helix of the secondary structure with Watson–Crick pairs.
Base-pair-step moves: -rna:denovo:bps_moves (helix flexibility by base pair step fragments).
Heat (-heat): Randomise torsions before assembly.
Close loops (-close_loops): Close chain breaks by cyclic coordinate descent after fragment moves.
Fuzz fragments: -fuzz_fragments value (0: not set).
Autofilter (-autofilter): Keep only models that score among the best during the run.
Filter low-res base pairs: -filter_lores_base_pairs: discard models missing the secondary-structure pairs.
Filter chain closure: -filter_chain_closure: discard models with open chain breaks.
… also halfway: -filter_chain_closure_halfway
… distance: -filter_chain_closure_distance (Å).
Coordinate constraints in minimiser: -rna:denovo:minimize:minimizer_use_coordinate_constraints
Dump PDBs (-rna:denovo:out:dump): Also write PDB files into each run folder.
Residues of the -s PDB: -input_res: residues provided by the fixed-helix PDB. Choices: typed, stems.
-input_res: Chain-qualified residues, e.g. 'A:1-6 A:13-16 B:17-20'.
Map resolution (-edensity:mapreso): Resolution of the connected map (Å).
Cryo-EM scatterers: -edensity:cryoem_scatterers (electron rather than X-ray form factors).
Density weight (elec_dens_fast): Score weight of the fit to the map.
coordinate_constraint: -set_weights coordinate_constraint (0: not set).
linear_chainbreak: -set_weights linear_chainbreak (0: not set).
Independent runs: Number of rna_denovo runs (seeds); each writes its own silent file.
Parallel runs: Runs started at the same time (xargs -P).
Reproducible seeds: -run:constant_seed with -run:jran <seed base + run number>.
Seed base: Run i uses seed base + i.
Run with nice: Lower the CPU priority of the runs.
rna_denovo executable: Name on PATH or full path, e.g. rna_denovo.default.linuxgccrelease.
Rosetta database: -database path (empty: found by the executable).
Extra flags: Additional rna_denovo flags, one or more per line (written to the flags file).
Conda environment: Activate this conda environment at the top of the script (eval "$(conda shell.bash hook)"; conda activate <name>). Leave empty when the programs are already on PATH.
Setup commands: Shell lines run before any program, e.g. 'module load ...' on a cluster or 'source /opt/amber26/amber.sh' on a workstation.
Cluster with rna_cluster: Group models by all-heavy-atom RMSD, best (lowest energy) cluster first. Off: rank all models of all runs by score.
Cluster radius (-cluster:radius): RMSD threshold (Å).
Maximum clusters (-nstruct)
Score window (-cluster:score_diff_cut): Only cluster models within this score of the best (empty: all).
rna_cluster executable
Extra rna_cluster flags
Models to extract: Cluster centres (or best models) written as PDB files <project>_<step>_model-01_<time>.pdb ...
extract_pdbs executable
Rosetta database: -database path (empty: found by the executables).
Annotate with x3dna-dssr: Base pairs, stems and secondary structure of every extracted model.
Also write JSON: x3dna-dssr --json output.
x3dna-dssr executable
Conda environment: Activate this conda environment at the top of the script (eval "$(conda shell.bash hook)"; conda activate <name>). Leave empty when the programs are already on PATH.
Setup commands: Shell lines run before any program, e.g. 'module load ...' on a cluster or 'source /opt/amber26/amber.sh' on a workstation.
GROMACS version: 2024+ on the workstation, 2023.3 on the cluster (loaded as a module). Choices: 2024, 2023.
Module to load: 'module load' line for the cluster version (empty: none).
gmx executable: gmx, gmx_mpi or a full path.
Convert Amber files with: ParmEd keeps off-diagonal Lennard-Jones pairs (NBfix) as [ nonbond_params ]; acpype is an alternative; 'none' uses GROMACS files as they are. Choices: parmed, acpype, none.

Hydrogen mass repartitioning (mdp): mass-repartition-factor = 3 in every mdp (GROMACS 2024+ only) so dt = 0.004 ps works with constraints = h-bonds. Not needed when the Amber topology already has HMR.
Restraint force constant: kJ/mol/nm² for stages with RNA position restraints.
Allow losing NBfix pairs: Normally the conversion stops when the Amber topology has off-diagonal LJ pairs that do not appear in the GROMACS topology.
Each stage starts from the previous stage's coordinates and checkpoint.
Name: Stage name used in file names (em, nvt, npt, md ...).
Integrator: steep: energy minimisation; md: leap-frog MD; sd: stochastic (Langevin) dynamics. Choices: steep, md, sd.
Steps (nsteps): Number of steps.
Force tolerance (emtol): Stop when the maximum force is below this (kJ/mol/nm).
Initial step (emstep): nm
Time step (dt): ps (0.004 needs hydrogen mass repartitioning).
Velocities: auto: generate after a minimisation, otherwise continue from the previous checkpoint. Choices: auto, new, continue.
Thermostat (tcoupl): Ignored by the sd integrator. Choices: V-rescale, Nose-Hoover, Berendsen.
Coupling groups (tc-grps): Thermostat groups; anything other than 'System' needs an index file.
tau-t: Thermostat time constant (ps); for sd the inverse friction.
Temperature (ref-t): K
Barostat (pcoupl): C-rescale works for equilibration and production; Parrinello-Rahman needs an equilibrated box. Choices: no, C-rescale, Parrinello-Rahman, Berendsen.
tau-p: Barostat time constant (ps).
Pressure (ref-p): bar
Compressibility: bar⁻¹ (water: 4.5e-5).
Constraints: Bonds constrained with LINCS. Choices: h-bonds, all-bonds, none.
Cutoff (rvdw = rcoulomb): nm (Amber force fields: 0.8-1.2).
RNA position restraints (-DPOSRES): Restrain nucleic-acid heavy atoms to the stage's starting coordinates.
Trajectory frame every: nstxout-compressed (0: none).
Energies every: nstenergy / nstlog.
Production stage: Its trajectory is passed on to analysis / visualisation steps.
Extra mdp lines: Added at the end of the mdp file (later lines override earlier ones).
Offload to the GPU: -nb gpu -pme gpu -bonded gpu
Update on the GPU (-update gpu): Fastest on one GPU; not available with every setting.
OpenMP threads (-ntomp): 0: let GROMACS decide.
grompp -maxwarn: Number of grompp warnings to accept.
Extra mdrun flags
Separate production script: Production stages go into their own script.
Conda environment: Activate this conda environment at the top of the script (eval "$(conda shell.bash hook)"; conda activate <name>). Leave empty when the programs are already on PATH.
Setup commands: Shell lines run before any program, e.g. 'module load ...' on a cluster or 'source /opt/amber26/amber.sh' on a workstation.
Text: Anything worth remembering about the plan.
File: The existing file. Relative paths are read from the folder of the saved preset.
Type: What the file contains; decides which inputs it can feed. Choices: pdb, fasta, secstruct, map, cif, smiles, silent, parm7, rst7, nc, dist, top, gro, xtc, trafl, image, text.
Clean with cpptraj first: Enable cpptraj stripping / imaging / fitting (Input & cleaning) when the paths are applied; solvated MD output normally needs it.
Phenix version: Installed Phenix release. Choices: 1.21, 2.x.
Phenix installation: Top folder of the Phenix installation; the script sources its phenix_env.sh. Leave empty when phenix.real_space_refine is already on PATH (or set it up below).
Resolution: Resolution of the map (required).
Macro cycles: macro_cycles of real_space_refine.
Global minimisation: run=minimization_global: Gradient-driven minimisation of the whole model against the map with geometry restraints.
Rigid body: run=rigid_body: Rigid-body refinement of the chains first (a model that is not yet placed well).
Local grid search: run=local_grid_search: Local real-space fitting of side chains / residues by grid search.
Morphing: run=morphing: Morphs the model towards the map: large, smooth moves of models from another state.
Simulated annealing: run=simulated_annealing: Real-space simulated annealing: larger radius of convergence, slower.
ADP (B-factors): run=adp: Refines atomic displacement parameters at the end.
Processors: nproc (parallel parts of the refinement).
Random seed: Empty: Phenix's default.
Output prefix: output.prefix of Phenix's files (empty: <project>_<step>_phenix-rsr_<time>); the refined model is copied to the step's own file.
Extra parameters: Appended verbatim to the command line, one or more per line (# starts a comment).
Nucleic-acid secondary-structure restraints: Phenix searches the model for base pairs and stacking and restrains them (secondary_structure.enabled=True).

Explicit base pairs: Written as base_pair restraints into a parameter (.eff) file. Dot-bracket: the connected secondary structure or the one typed below (nothing is written when there is none). Annotation: the REMARK 950 PAIR records of the model ('mdatk pdb annotate'), read when the files are written. Choices: none, secstruct, annotation.
Sequence: For a typed dot-bracket (chains separated by spaces).
Dot-bracket: Ignored when a secondary structure is connected.

Residue numbering: How dot-bracket positions map to residues: the nucleotides of the model in file order (when it exists; otherwise continuous numbering), numbers continuous across chains from 1, or restarting at 1 in every chain. Choices: model, continuous, chain.
Restrain G·U wobble pairs: Saenger class 28.
Stacking from the annotation: Also write the STACK records as stacking_pair restraints.

Setup commands: Shell lines run before any program, e.g. 'module load ...' on a cluster or 'source /opt/amber26/amber.sh' on a workstation.
Coot version: Installed Coot generation; the script works in both, the version selects the command-line flags. Choices: 0.9, 1.x.
Coot executable: Name or path of the coot program.
Residues: Residue ranges to refine, e.g. 'A:1-20, B:5-12' (empty: every polymer residue; a range without a chain applies to every chain).
Zone size: Residues refined together (refine_zone window).
Zone overlap: Residues shared by neighbouring windows.
Cycles: Passes over all windows.
Map weight: Default: Coot's own weight. Auto: auto_weight_for_refinement (when this Coot has it). Fixed: set_matrix with the value below. Choices: default, auto, fixed.
Weight: set_matrix value (larger: the map pulls harder).
Torsion restraints: set_refine_with_torsion_restraints: also restrain torsions from the dictionaries.
